dedupe_keys.name: ashrae global thermal comfort database ii

description: The ASHRAE Global Thermal Comfort Database II pairs objective indoor environmental measurements with right-here-right-now thermal comfort votes from occupants of buildings around the world. Launched in 2014 under UC Berkeley's Center for the Built Environment and the University of Sydney's IEQ Laboratory, it harmonised raw data from two decades of field studies: 77,304 quality-assured rows, 25,288 rows from the earlier ASHRAE RP-884 database, and 6,441 rows added in version 2.1, for 109,033 entries. Columns cover building and study metadata (region, country, city, climate, season, building type, cooling strategy, publication, contributor), subject age, gender, height and weight, measured air, radiant, operative and globe temperatures at several heights, humidity and air speed, clothing and metabolic rate, thermal sensation, acceptability and preference votes with PMV, PPD and SET, use of windows, doors, fans, blinds and heaters, and outdoor weather from nearby stations. Coverage: field studies worldwide in many building types. Access: CSV downloads on Dryad and GitHub, with the code used to build each version since 2.1. Licence: CC BY 4.0 on Dryad; free. Caveats: studies used different instruments and protocols, and some building identifiers are inferred. Simulation uses are calibrating and testing thermal comfort models, adaptive comfort limits for heat resilience and control strategies. Related records: the ASHRAE Global Occupant Behavior Database.
